results.title: Fujian: Market Profile | HKTDC Research
results.content: ## Data and Profiles - Chinese Mainland Provinces and Cities - Provinces. # Fujian: Market Profile. Fujian is located in the south eastern coast, opposite to Taiwan. The Southeast Fujian (閩東南) area which comprises five cities and counties ‑‑ Fuzhou (福州), Xiamen (廈門), Putian (莆田), Quanzhou (泉州) and Zhangzhou (漳州), is the economic hub of Fujian, accounting for 78% of the province’s GDP in 2023. In 2004, Fujian proposed the “Westbank Economic Zone”(海峽西岸經濟區) strategy, a zone along the west coast of the Taiwan Straits (including parts of Guangdong and Zhejiang provinces) for socio‑economic development. In May 2009, the State Council passed the Several Opinions on Supporting Fuijian Province to Accelerate Construction of the Economic Zone West of the Taiwan Straits. The China (Fujian) Pilot Free Trade Zone (FJFTZ) was officially launched in April 2015. In 2023, Major export markets included the US, Philippines, Taiwan and Japan. Hong Kong was the ninth major export market of Fujian, accounting for 3.29% of the province’s total exports. Fujian’s major export items included Machinery and transport equipment, finished products classified by raw materials, electrical machinery, devices and appliances etc. In 2023, major import sources included Australia, Taiwan, the US and Japan. Hong Kong is the largest source of FDI in Fujian, accounting for 24.14% of the province’s utilised FDI in 2023, followed by Cayman Islands as the second major investment source. In terms of number of foreign‑invested enterprises registered, the manufacturing sector accounted for 24.14% of the total in 2023, followed by leasing and business services at 12.98%. results.title: Fujian Ranks 7th in Big Data Development in China --Among the First Echelon in the Country
results.content: ## Fujian Ranks 7th in Big Data Development in China --Among the First Echelon in the Country. ##### From：Fujian International Investment Promotion Center Date：2022-08-22【Font：large) regular;)】. Recently, the CCID Information and Software Industry Research Institute has officially published the "Evaluation Report on China's Regional Development of Big Data (2022)". According to the report, Fujian ranks 7th in big data development in the country, entering the first echelon. Centering around the three key dimensions of the basic environment, industry development and integrated application, relevant typical indexes were selected in the report to carry out evaluation and analysis of development in areas such as the big data policy system, industrial foundation, industrial chain, and ecological system in 31 cities, districts and provinces across the country. Based on various indexes for evaluating the regional development of big data, the top seven provinces or cities are Guangdong, Beijing, Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Shandong and Fujian. It is pointed out in the report that these seven provinces or cities demonstrate distinctive advantages and lead the country in resources and comprehensive strength. Among these, Fujian encourages coordination of top leader responsibility and Chief Data Officer in its development of the big data industry, ranking top in the country in terms of the policy landscape and organizational structure and showing notable results in developing soft and hard environments. In addition, efforts are made in facilitating in-depth integration of industry chain and innovation chain, accelerating construction of systems for data resources and promoting key industry applications, which ensure steady growth of Fujian's big data industry. The report also points out that the big data industry of Fujian still has considerable room for improvement in application in government affairs and industries. results.title: China to pilot digital yuan in more cities--China Economic Net
results.content: China to pilot digital yuan in more cities. Last Updated: 2022-04-03 00:43 | Xinhua. Photo taken on May 8, 2021 shows a digital Chinese yuan payment card used at the first China International Consumer Products Expo in Haikou, capital of south China's Hainan Province. China's central bank announced Saturday that its digital yuan pilot program will be expanded to more domestic cities following its successful operation over the past years. The digital fiat currency, or e-CNY, will be accessible in Tianjin and Chongqing municipalities, Guangzhou in south China's Guangdong Province, Fuzhou and Xiamen in east China's Fujian Province, and six cities in east China's Zhejiang Province hosting the 2022 Asian Games, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said in a statement. The country has tested the use of the digital yuan in over 10 places from Shenzhen to Shanghai and Xiong'an New Area. results.title: Fujian | History, Province, Cities, Population, & Facts | Britannica
results.content: # Fujian. Fujian (meaning “Happy Establishment”) is one of the country’s smaller provinces, but it occupies a strategic maritime position between the two sections of the China Sea. Its capital and largest city is Fuzhou (“Happy City”). Along that boundary run the Wuyi Mountains, which, in the extreme north, include the Xianxia Mountains on the Zhejiang-Fujian border. The Wuyi Mountains, which form a formidable natural barrier between Fujian and the interior of China, reach an elevation of about 6,000 feet (1,800 metres) in western Fujian and in adjacent parts of southwest Zhejiang. The drainage area of the Min River of Fujian (to be distinguished from the Min River of Sichuan province) covers about half of the province. To the southwest of the Min is the Han River, which crosses the southwestern border of Fujian province to empty into the sea at Shantou (Swatow), the main port of eastern Guangdong. In western Fujian the lower elevations support tropical mountain forests.

results.title: Consulate General of India, Guangzhou : Fujian
results.content: While Fuzhou is the capital of Fujian province, the more southern Xiamen is one of China’s four original special economic zones (along with Guangzhou province’s Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Shantou) and a key trade hub-its port and airport are both the third busiest in the region, behind Guangzhou and Shenzhen. Fujian provincial government has a standing policy to promote the development of emerging industries, including new generation information technology, biotechnology and new medicine, new materials, new energy, energy-saving, high-end equipment manufacturing, and the marine high-tech industry. Fujian will fully initiate its marine economy pilot projects in 2013, targeting the total output value of the industry at RMB 730 billion by 2015, taking up more than 28 percent of the total regional production value and eventually turning itself into a powerful province of marine economy by 2020. Fujian’s 12th Five Year Plan encourages foreign investment towards newly emerging strategic industries, modern service industries, energy saving and environmental protection industries, and other key industries. Fujian’s development zones received great attention under China’s 11th Five Year Plan, in which the State Council approved free trade port zones both in Xiamen and Fuzhou and upgraded three provincial development zones – China Merchants Zhangzhou Development Zone, Quanzhou Economic and Technological Development Zone, Quanzhou High-tech Industrial Development Zone – to state level status. Autoparts are a major product in Fujian province and this is no more clearly seen than in Hua’an Economic Development Zone, which is home to the “aluminum wheel production project.” According to Fujian government plans, this zone will develop an auto spare parts industrial cluster that produces car wheels, car bearings, tires as well as auto glass products, among others. The West Coast Economic Zone (also known as the Western Taiwan Straits Economic Zone) covers the entirety of Fujian province, as well as several cities in the Zhejiang, Guangdong, and Jiangxi provinces. The Zone, described in China’s 12th Five Year Plan, was proposed by the Fujian government and Chinese central government with the purpose of facilitating political and economic relationships across the Taiwan Straits and accelerating economic development along the coastal cities in Fujian province.
